turns.question: Where can we get coffee and hot chocolate in Wakefield city centre?
turns.reply:
There are several good spots in central Wakefield for coffee and hot chocolate. Here are five options:

Bob & Berts (Trinity Walk), all-day cafe with coffee, hot chocolate, brunch and lighter food. Opens 7:30am weekdays, 9am Sunday. Seating available.

Starbucks (Trinity Walk), standard chain option, also does hot chocolate and cakes. Opens 7am weekdays, 8am Sunday, closes 7pm most days.

Costa Coffee (Northgate), another reliable chain choice for coffee and hot chocolate. Opens 8am, closes 6pm weekdays and 4pm Sunday.

KRA:FT Koffee (Wood Street), independent coffee shop. Opens Tuesday to Friday 8am–3pm, Saturday 8am–4pm, Sunday 10am–3pm. Closed Mondays.

Caffé Nero (Trinity Walk), coffee-focused with hot chocolate available. Opens 7:30am weekdays and Saturday, 8am Sunday, closes 6:30pm most days.

All of these are of each other in the city centre. Bob & Berts and Starbucks tend to have more seating if you want to settle in for a bit.

turns.question: How do I report a pothole?
turns.reply:
You can report a pothole to Wakefield Council online at wakefield.gov.uk/potholes. 

For out-of-hours emergencies, call 01924 306 987.

For official and up-to-date information, visit wakefield.gov.uk or call 0345 8 506 506.

turns.question: Where can I find a library?
turns.reply:
Wakefield has several libraries across the district. The main one is Wakefield Library in the city centre at Castle Street, WF1 1PU.

Other libraries include branches in Ossett, Horbury, Castleford, Pontefract and other district towns.

For current opening hours, services, events and the full list of locations, check wakefield.gov.uk/libraries or call 0345 8 506 506 (Mon–Fri 8:30am–5pm).
